clue.text: Californian banker makes entreaty after Eucharist

indicators.note: the cry is placed after the rite, so it comes at the end of the word

parts.note: the Eucharist is a Christian sacrament, here the general word for such a rite
O is the exclamation of pleading, as in 'O, spare me'

explanation.surface: A Californian bank manager pleads with the congregation after Communion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' is crossword slang for a river (it has banks); the Sacramento flows through California.
explanation.definitionFit: A river has banks, so a Californian river is a Californian banker in crossword idiom.

clue.text: Fire and plunder

explanation.surface: An army that burns and loots a town.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss from a job is to sack; to loot a captured town is also to sack it.

clue.text: Take steps to provide tea for three

parts.note: char or cha is British slang for tea; three servings give it three times
char or cha is British slang for tea; three servings give it three times
char or cha is British slang for tea; three servings give it three times

explanation.surface: An invitation to pour a pot of tea for three guests.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin dance is done by taking steps, so dancing it is literally taking steps.

clue.text: Make trouble after current set-back

parts.note: AC is alternating current

indicators.note: back says the word for set is read in reverse

parts.note: to set something down is to put it

explanation.surface: Someone causes a scene after a setback with the electricity supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-back' looks like one word meaning a reverse, but splits into the verb and its reversal signal; 'after' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To misbehave or malfunction, an idiom for causing a fuss or not working properly.

clue.text: Secular novice in crude accommodation

indicators.note: in places the novice inside the word for crude, which gives it accommodation

parts.note: earthy humour is crude, vulgar
L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A trainee monk is lodged in rough, primitive quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodation' backs up 'in': the crude word houses the novice.
explanation.definitionFit: Worldly as opposed to spiritual; secular matters concern this world rather than heaven.

clue.text: Tory leader criticised for being outmanoeuvred

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of Tory

parts.note: to rap someone is to rebuke them

explanation.surface: The Conservative leader, attacked in the press, has been outflanked by rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone outmanoeuvred is caught with no escape, cornered.

clue.text: Crack shot

explanation.surface: A sharpshooter fires one expert round.
explanation.definitionFit: A twig cracks with a sudden break; a quick photograph is also called this.

clue.text: Seen to be upset about many basic requirements

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go round the numeral
upset says the letters of seen are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
D is the Roman numeral for 500, crossword shorthand for many

explanation.surface: Being seen upset over many essential things.
explanation.walkthrough: SEEN rearranged gives NEES, which goes 'about' D.
explanation.definitionFit: Necessities: the things one requires are one's wants or necessaries.

clue.text: Expert ex-teacher

parts.note: ex means former, in the past
a schoolmaster is a teacher

explanation.surface: A retired teacher who knows their stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone thoroughly skilled at something is called an old hand or virtuoso, this idiom.

clue.text: Given credit for having made headway

explanation.surface: A borrower is lent money for having made progress.
explanation.definitionFit: A loan paid up front is money advanced; something that has moved forward has also advanced.

clue.text: Carol may not embrace Henry

indicators.note: embrace says one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: can't means is not able, may not
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A woman named Carol is not allowed to hug a man called Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: Carol reads as a woman's name but is the verb, to sing.
explanation.definitionFit: To carol is to sing joyfully, as is to intone a song.

clue.text: Apply oneself anew to study costume

parts.note: to read a subject at university is to study it
a dress is a garment, a costume

explanation.surface: A drama student returns to research the costume for a play.
explanation.definitionFit: To address a task is to apply oneself to it; doing that again is the re- form.

clue.text: Quickly produced two slices of meat

parts.note: a chop is a cut of meat, and there are two of them
a chop is a cut of meat, and there are two of them

explanation.surface: A butcher swiftly cuts two pieces of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pidgin expression urging speed, meaning hurry up.

clue.text: A multitude returning from Indian state

indicators.note: returning says the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a mass is a large crowd, a multitude

explanation.surface: Huge crowds come home from a region of India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses A MASS into SSAM A.
explanation.definitionFit: A state in north-east India, famous for its tea.

clue.text: Out of trouble whilst sailing past south west Holland

parts.note: a ship lying just beyond a coast is off it
the Hook of Holland is a port in the south-west of the Netherlands

explanation.surface: A ship cruises past a port on the Dutch coast and avoids danger.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for escaping blame or obligation, like a fish released.

clue.text: Works to disclose division of unknown quantity

parts.note: a factor is a divisor, a number that divides into another
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Mathematicians work to reveal how an unknown number divides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' is a noun, a plant; 'to disclose' is a link saying the wordplay reveals it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant where goods are made is called the works.

clue.text: A bloomer no dealer made

indicators.note: made in the sense of formed into something new from these letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gaffe that a card dealer never makes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder, but it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that flowers is a bloomer; this evergreen shrub has showy pink blooms.

clue.text: A famous writer? The devil it is!

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise about a celebrated novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles of that surname wrote Oliver Twist; 'what the dickens' is an old oath where the word replaces devil.

clue.text: I created a disturbance to cause destruction

indicators.note: a disturbance stirs the letters into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to causing a commotion that ended in ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: To destroy completely, wipe out, is to bring about destruction.

clue.text: Essay about ancient drama

indicators.note: about says the attempt wraps round the word for old

parts.note: to essay is to try, attempt
aged means old, ancient

explanation.surface: A student writes a paper on Greek theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ancient drama' looks like the definition, but 'ancient' is wordplay; the definition is just 'drama'.
explanation.definitionFit: A play with an unhappy ending is a kind of drama.

clue.text: CID to carry weapons on board ship

parts.note: the Criminal Investigation Department of Scotland Yard is called the Yard
to arm is to equip with weapons

explanation.surface: Detectives arm themselves before boarding a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A spar end on a sailing mast, part of a ship's rigging.

clue.text: Left-wing video exposes excessive formality

parts.note: red is the colour of socialism
a videotape is a video

explanation.surface: A socialist film lays bare bureaucratic obstruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Bureaucracy is named after the coloured ribbon once used to tie official papers.

clue.text: Determination to find another answer

explanation.surface: A strong will to work out a different solution.
explanation.definitionFit: Firmness of purpose is resolve; to work out a problem a second time is to re-solve it.

clue.text: Urge to see one's breakfast cooking?

explanation.surface: A wry question about watching one's breakfast boil.
explanation.definitionFit: To incite or encourage is to urge someone; an egg on the stove is literally cooking.

clue.text: Managed to travel over 100mph

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece stands above the second

parts.note: to go is to travel
a ton is a speed of 100mph in British slang

explanation.surface: A driver manages to break a speed of a hundred miles an hour.
explanation.definitionFit: To get on is to fare or cope, so one who got on managed.

clue.text: Use a filter again to check

explanation.surface: Advice to re-filter something as a check.
explanation.definitionFit: Straining a second time is re-straining; to hold back is to check.

clue.text: Butler and bishop meet one religious leader

parts.note: Rab Butler was a British Conservative statesman
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A manservant and a bishop meet one cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: Butler is the surname of Rab Butler, a leading British politician of the 1950s and 60s, not a manservant.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish teacher and leader of a congregation.

clue.text: Beat the unbeatable

explanation.surface: Defeat the team nobody can defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo someone is to best them; the finest is the unbeatable top.

clue.text: How to apply cosmetic varnish pronto

explanation.surface: Instructions for painting nails quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Polish goes on the fingernail; paying 'on the nail' means paying immediately.

clue.text: A couple need support

explanation.surface: Partners who need to prop each other up.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of game birds is a brace; a prop or strut is also a brace.

clue.text: Some pupils work industriously in class

indicators.note: some says only part of these words is taken, a run inside them

explanation.surface: A few pupils work hard during lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind is a sort or category, as is a class.

clue.text: One-metre gable causes an obstruction

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a pediment is the triangular gable over a classical portico

explanation.surface: A small gable of one metre gets in the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A hindrance or barrier is an impediment.
